History of Aboriginals

Aboriginal Symbols Illustration

The “U” shape on the ground symbolizes a person sitting cross-legged. Lines linking circles illustrate the paths taken by people as they move from one site to another.

Women Symbol

The combination of a coolamon bowl and a digging stick forms a symbol resembling “UOI”, signifying a woman engaged in hunting or gathering.

Gathering Symbol

The arrangement of spears and possibly boomerangs can be visually represented as “U ||”, indicating a male figure.

Aboriginal Map Symbols

This picture provides a detailed understanding of Aboriginal maps, marking what each drawing represents:

2. Sand Hills
3. Fire
4. Bush fire
5. Burnt Country
6. Spinifex Grass
7. River
8. Sticks and Branches
9. Dry Water Holes
10. Bush Tucker
11. Caves
12. Fighting Stick
13. Ceremonial Belts
14. Wirra kurru
15. Water Holes
16. Women with Digging Sticks
17. Coolamon Bowls
